title: Cross-cycle pairing matrix and elastic buffer playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: We routinely hit mid-cycle execution risk when multiple initiatives overlap and teams have asymmetric skills. Current approaches (fixed buffer FTE or ad-hoc reassignments) are either too blunt or too slow. Proposal: build a lightweight playbook and tooling pattern that combines (1) a cross-cycle pairing matrix (role/skill pairings + week-level overlap schedule) and (2) an elastic FTE buffer with clear allocation, activation triggers, and rollback rules. The goal is to reduce scope drift and emergency rework while preserving team autonomy and minimizing context-switch cost.

Scope: playbook text, example pairing matrices, pilot process with two squads (Infra and Console), a small allocation policy (0.5–1.5 FTE buffer per tranche), and dashboards to track buffer utilization and decision triggers. Not building full automation in this cycle — deliverables are a playbook + spreadsheet + dashboard queries + pilot retrospective.

Out-of-scope: full org-level FTE reassignments, compensation changes, or HR-level role changes. This is an operational protocol for cycles only.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook document published on Confluence with examples and step-by-step activation flow
Pairing matrix template (xlsx) with mapping for at least two pilot squads and one cross-functional critical skill (e.g., kernel scheduling)
Dashboard queries that surface buffer utilization, percent of weeks with >0.75 buffer utilization, and scope-slippage events linked to buffer activation
Pilot run completed for 1 cycle with retrospective notes and at least two measurable improvements (reduced unplanned rollbacks or faster incident triage)
Clear activation/rollback criteria defined (percent utilization, SLA breach, or on-call page thresholds)
decisions: Pilot first with Infra and Console teams for 6 weeks (decision: reduces coordination overhead)
Elastic buffer staffed as fractional FTE pool (0.5–1.5 per tranche) rather than full-team shadowing to minimize context switching
Pairing matrix will prioritize critical cross-cutting skills (serving runtime kernel ops, autoscaler tuning, and rollout testing) and map primary+secondary owners for each week
